value.body: Brands, agencies, news outlets and creators hire people to write, shoot, edit and publish content for websites, newsletters, YouTube and social platforms. Roles include content writer, social media executive, video editor, digital producer and community manager.

items.label: Entry requirement
items.note: No licence; a journalism or mass communication degree helps but is not required

items.label: Common roles
items.value: Content writer, social media executive, video editor, digital producer

items.label: Core skills
items.value: Writing, short video, platform analytics, basic design

items.label: Journalism & mass communication UG students
items.note: Undergraduate enrolment in this subject; many people in digital content come from other degrees

items.label: Journalism & mass communication UG pass-outs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Build a portfolio — published articles, a running social account, videos or campaign samples — and apply to agencies, media houses and brand teams. Internships during the degree are a common entry route.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry-level pay is often modest, and agency work can be deadline-heavy.
Platform rules and algorithms change, so skills need regular updating.
Paths lead to editor, content strategist, brand or digital marketing roles.

value.title: UG students in Journalism & Mass Communication
value.note: One common degree route into this field; many people enter digital content work from other degrees or without one. AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 12 (UG level), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
